discovery: The cold dark matter theory of hierarchical galaxy and structure formation

nominees.name: Simon D. M. White
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Martin J. Rees
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Astronomy, University of Cambridge, United Kingdom

nominees.name: Sandra M. Faber
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Santa Cruz, USA

motivation: White and Rees (1978) proposed that galaxies form by gas cooling and condensing inside hierarchically merging dark matter halos. Blumenthal, Faber, Primack and Rees (1984) then showed that cold, non-baryonic dark matter explains the masses and structure of galaxies and the large-scale distribution of matter. White led the numerical programme that made this framework testable. Simulations showed that neutrino dark matter fails, while cold dark matter reproduces galaxy clustering, the cosmic web and universal halo profiles. Faber's observational work tied the theory to real galaxies. Together they built the paradigm, now confirmed by CMB, galaxy-survey and lensing data, that says most matter is a new, non-baryonic particle and that it drove the formation of all cosmic structure. This is a key clue to physics beyond the Standard Model and changed how we understand the contents and structure of the Universe.
